title: Spaced repetition: the highest-ROI revision habit
excerpt: Why spacing your revision beats cramming every time — and how StudYear automates it for GCSE and A-Level.
metaDesc: Spaced repetition is the highest-ROI revision habit for GCSE and A-Level. Learn how the science works and how StudYear schedules it for you automatically.
body:
Cramming feels productive, but the evidence is blunt: what you learn the night before is mostly gone within a week. **Spaced repetition** — revisiting material at widening intervals — is the single highest-return revision habit a student can build.

## Why spacing beats cramming
Each time you retrieve a fact just as you are about to forget it, the memory is rebuilt stronger and the next forgetting curve is flatter. The [Education Endowment Foundation](https://educationendowmentfoundation.org.uk/) rates retrieval and spaced practice among the most cost-effective ways to raise attainment.

## How to apply it in a week
- Study a topic today, then again in 2 days, then 5, then 10.
- Keep each session short — 15–20 minutes of active recall, not passive re-reading.
- Test yourself from a blank page before you check your notes.

## How StudYear does it for you
Our [Smart Review](/study/) engine tracks what you have learned and resurfaces anything at risk of being forgotten, automatically — no scheduling spreadsheet required. Pair it with the [SkillRush fluency arena](/skillrush/) to make weak facts automatic. See [how StudYear works](/how-it-works/) or start with a [free assessment](/study/).

## FAQ
### Is spaced repetition better than re-reading?
Yes. Actively retrieving information from memory, spaced over days, produces far stronger long-term recall than re-reading or highlighting.
### How many days should I space my revision?
A simple, effective schedule is day 1, day 3, day 8 and day 16 — widening the gap each time you get it right.

Yes — the Smart Review tab surfaces topics you are about to forget, so you never have to plan the intervals yourself.

title: Choosing GCSE options: a Year 9 parent's guide
excerpt: How to help your child pick GCSE subjects that keep the most doors open — based on strengths, not guesswork.
metaDesc: A practical Year 9 guide to choosing GCSE options: how to pick subjects by strength, keep post-16 routes open, and use StudYear's Career Passport to decide.
body:
Choosing GCSE options is the first big fork in a child's education — and most families make it with too little information. Here is how to decide with confidence.

## Start with strengths, not subjects
Better grades come from subjects a child is genuinely good at and enjoys. Look at real evidence — recent assessment scores — rather than what friends are picking.

## Keep doors open
The English Baccalaureate core (English, maths, science, a language and a humanity) keeps the widest range of post-16 routes available. For the official rules, see [GOV.UK on the EBacc](https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/english-baccalaureate-ebacc).

## Match choices to where they might go
From 2028 the government is putting technical routes on an equal footing with academic ones, so a child can combine strong GCSEs with a clear line into an apprenticeship, T-Level or university.

## Use the evidence you already have
StudYear's [Career Passport](/career/) maps a child's real strengths to best-fit GCSE options and post-16 routes, and our [tutor marketplace](/tutors/) can shore up any subject that needs lifting before the deadline. New to StudYear? [See how it works](/how-it-works/).

## FAQ
### What GCSEs keep the most options open?
The EBacc core — English, maths, the sciences, a language and a humanities subject — keeps the widest set of A-level, apprenticeship and university routes available.
### Should my child pick subjects they enjoy or subjects that look impressive?
Enjoyment and strength usually win: children work harder and score higher in subjects they like, and good grades open more doors than an impressive-looking but poorly-graded subject.
### How does StudYear help with GCSE choices?
The Career Passport turns a child's real assessment data into recommended GCSE options and post-16 pathways, so the decision is based on evidence rather than guesswork.

title: How schools can evidence the Gatsby Benchmarks automatically
excerpt: The 8 Gatsby Benchmarks are statutory — here's how to evidence them from data your school already generates.
metaDesc: Every English secondary is measured on the 8 Gatsby Benchmarks. Learn what they are and how StudYear evidences them automatically from your existing data.
body:
Careers provision is no longer a nice-to-have — it is statutory, and with the 14+ technical-education reforms it is about to carry more weight in inspection. The framework schools are measured against is the **Gatsby Benchmarks**.

## What the benchmarks ask for
The eight benchmarks cover a stable careers programme, good labour-market information, personal guidance, and — the hardest to evidence — real encounters with employers and experiences of workplaces. The [Careers & Enterprise Company](https://www.careersandenterprise.co.uk/) sets out the detail.

## Why evidence is the bottleneck
Most schools deliver plenty of activity but struggle to *prove* it at inspection. Encounters happen; the audit trail does not always follow.

## Turn activity into an evidence pack
StudYear's [school careers tools](/school/) compute live Gatsby coverage from the employer encounters, business projects and work experience your staff log — and export an inspection-ready pack in one click. It pairs with the student [Career Passport](/career/) so pupil and school data line up. [See how it works](/how-it-works/).

## FAQ
### Are the Gatsby Benchmarks statutory?
Every English secondary school must have regard to the eight Gatsby Benchmarks and is measured against them, so in practice they function as a statutory standard for careers provision.
### Which Gatsby Benchmark is hardest to evidence?
Benchmarks 5 and 6 — encounters with employers and experiences of workplaces — are usually the hardest, because the activity happens but the evidence trail is often incomplete.
### How does StudYear evidence the benchmarks?
It computes coverage automatically from the encounters, projects and work experience staff log, then exports an inspection-ready evidence pack.
